title: Latent Hatred: A Benchmark for Understanding Implicit Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability of models to detect implicit hate speech directed at various groups, including religious groups. It specifically collected and annotated data from hate groups with an 'Anti-Muslim' ideology. The evaluation included classifying text into categories of implicit hate (e.g., Stereotypes and Misinformation, which includes holocaust denial) and generating explanations for the hateful content, including the targeted group.
findings: The study identified 'Anti-Muslim' as one of the major ideological clusters of U.S. hate groups. It found that models struggle with coded hate symbols, including the anti-Semitic symbol '(((they)))'. Furthermore, models exhibited 'identity term bias,' tending to overclassify tweets containing terms like 'Jew' as hateful speech, indicating difficulty in distinguishing between identity mentions and actual hate.
